Summary

Data source overview:  
The document is MIRI’s comprehensive “2015 in review” report.  It surveys why misaligned advanced AI is risky, identifies six technical failure modes that could lead to that risk, describes 2015 research results that tackle each failure mode, and implicitly motivates future work that will turn these results into implementable safety mechanisms.

Inference strategy justification:  
The paper is a retrospective; it rarely states “and therefore do X” explicitly.  Where a direct engineering step was not spelled-out, I applied light inference (confidence level 2) to turn each research result into the most obvious AI-safety intervention an engineer or researcher would attempt next (e.g. “train safely interruptible agents”).  These interventions are faithful to the intent of the cited work and keep maturity ratings low (1–2).

Extraction completeness explanation:  
All six core risk mechanisms named or clearly implied in the text (logical uncertainty, self-reference, corrigibility, excessive maximization, value specification, multi-agent cooperation) are represented as failure-mode concept nodes.  Every 2015 research contribution that the report claims as progress toward solving those mechanisms is captured as a theoretical-framework concept node, and every such framework is linked to an actionable intervention node.  The resulting graph contains 22 tightly-connected nodes—well above the minimum information density while remaining readable.

Key limitations:  
1. The report spans many distinct sub-papers; some fine details (e.g. exact algorithmic pseudocode) are necessarily abstracted.  
2. The maturity levels are estimates because no uniform TRL scale is given in the report.  
3. Some cross-dependencies between frameworks (e.g. logical uncertainty enabling better corrigibility) are plausible but not explicitly documented and therefore omitted.
